import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/test_9.csv"
]

# Corresponding target column suffixes for SalePrice columns in the target table
# According to the target schema:
# SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y, SalePrice_x_3, SalePrice_y_4, SalePrice_x_5, SalePrice_y_6, SalePrice_x_7, SalePrice_y_8, SalePrice_x_9, SalePrice_y_10
# We have 10 SalePrice columns from 10 source tables.
# The pattern of suffixes is:
# Source 0 -> SalePrice_x
# Source 1 -> SalePrice_y
# Source 2 -> SalePrice_x_3
# Source 3 -> SalePrice_y_4
# Source 4 -> SalePrice_x_5
# Source 5 -> SalePrice_y_6
# Source 6 -> SalePrice_x_7
# Source 7 -> SalePrice_y_8
# Source 8 -> SalePrice_x_9
# Source 9 -> SalePrice_y_10

target_saleprice_cols = [
    "SalePrice_x",
    "SalePrice_y",
    "SalePrice_x_3",
    "SalePrice_y_4",
    "SalePrice_x_5",
    "SalePrice_y_6",
    "SalePrice_x_7",
    "SalePrice_y_8",
    "SalePrice_x_9",
    "SalePrice_y_10"
]

# Step 1: Load all source tables into dataframes with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# Step 2: Rename the SalePrice column in each dataframe to the corresponding target SalePrice column name
for i, df in enumerate(dfs):
    df.rename(columns={"SalePrice": target_saleprice_cols[i]}, inplace=True)

# Step 3: Merge all dataframes on 'Id' column using inner join to keep only Ids present in all sources
# This is because the target table has 729 rows, which matches the size of Source 1 (729 tuples),
# so inner join will reduce to the intersection of all Ids.
merged_df = dfs[0]
for df in dfs[1:]:
    merged_df = pd.merge(merged_df, df, on="Id", how="inner")

# Step 4: Ensure the final dataframe columns are in the exact order of the target schema
target_columns = ["Id"] + target_saleprice_cols
merged_df = merged_df[target_columns]

# Step 5: Cast columns to the target data types
merged_df["Id"] = merged_df["Id"].astype(int)
for col in target_saleprice_cols:
    merged_df[col] = merged_df[col].astype(float)

# Step 6: Write the resulting dataframe to the target CSV file without the index
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/target_multisource_cot.csv"
merged_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
